item.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. For every closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$, its open interior $V=\prod_{i<3}(a_i,b_i)$ is a volume test geometry and $\overline V=K$. Its natural six-face presentation is the boundary of $K$, with outward normals $\pm e_i$. The volume variable is $V$, while $K$ denotes its compact closure. Each face is a degenerate three-dimensional box and hence has $\lambda_3$-measure zero by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]; their finite union $K\setminus V$ is null. Thus for continuous $h$ on a neighbourhood of $K$, $\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3=\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$: the positive and negative integrals over the null difference vanish by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]].

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
item.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the open box interior, with compact closure $K$, is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus. The requirement $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ makes clause (c)'s existing neighbourhood requirement explicit and restores the canonical definition contract. The closed-box integral bridge follows from the six degenerate faces being volume-null and the signed-integral definition, independently of their nonzero surface areas.

item.title: Distributional Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface inherited from [[def-em-surface-distribution]] ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units and constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $\mathcal D'(U)$ be the space of distributions on $U$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); recall that the pairing $\langle T,\psi\rangle$ is bilinear with no conjugation and that the distributional partial derivatives are $\langle\partial_\mu T,\psi\rangle=-\langle T,\partial_\mu\psi\rangle$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(a) [Fields as distributions] Locally integrable fields and source densities on $U$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]).

(b) [Point sources] Let $I_0\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, let $z:I_0\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$ is proper into the open set $U$, and let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs). By [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]],
$$\langle\rho_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}\psi(z(t),t)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_{\mathrm{pt}},\psi\rangle:=q\int_{I_0}z'(t)\,\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$ with $\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$. If instead $I_0=(a,b)$ has finite endpoints, $z$ extends continuously to $[a,b]$, the absolute improper integral $\int_a^b|z'(t)|\,dt$ is finite and both endpoint events lie in $U$, the same formulas define distributions with
$$\partial_t\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}+\operatorname{div}J_{\mathrm{pt}}=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$$
([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]); a finite-history point source therefore contributes an endpoint term unless that term is included explicitly, and the pairings above exclude it only by the stated properness or endpoint hypotheses.

(c) [Stationary-sheet sources] Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density; the sheet is stationary). Then
$$\langle\rho_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_S\sigma(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt,\qquad \langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=\int_I\int_SK(x,t)\psi(x,t)\,dS(x)\,dt$$
define distributions on $U$: for $\psi$ with compact support the inner integrals are continuous in $t$ on a compact parameter interval and the functionals are bounded by $(\sup|\sigma\psi|)\,\mathrm{area}(S)\,\mathrm{length}$ of the time projection of the support, and likewise in the vector case. A normal sheet current (one with $K\cdot n\ne0$), a line current and a moving sheet are not source types of this definition.

(d) [Unrestricted weak fields and optional interface branches] The general field class for the solution predicate (e) consists of all locally integrable pairs $(E,B)$ on $U$, also when the source has a stationary-sheet part. No classical one-sided trace or off-sheet $C^1$ regularity is required to define those four distributional pairings. Additional trace hypotheses are optional hypotheses of interface/jump results, not admission requirements of the general weak model.
For a pointwise classical jump branch, one may additionally assume that $E,B$ are $C^1$ off $S\times I$ and, around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighborhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. These joint one-sided extensions make the field traces and first spatial/temporal derivatives continuous up to that side, locally uniformly on compact cylinders.
For the broader weak-trace branch, one may instead assume the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, with the explicit additional conditions that the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ for $dSdt$. This branch supports sheet-distribution and almost-everywhere jump identities; spatial continuity at each time gives pointwise spatial identities for almost every time, and joint continuity of the jump densities gives the further all-time upgrade. Separate spatial $C^1$ traces at each time alone do not imply that joint regularity or upgrade. Whenever such traces exist, $[F]:=F_+-F_-$ denotes their jump in the chosen normal convention. (e) [Weak Maxwell equations with a distributional source pair] Let $E,B$ be a field pair of class (d), let $\rho=\rho_v+\rho_s$ and $J=J_v+J_s$ be source distributions on $U$ whose volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are locally integrable volume densities with the charge/current quantity types of [[def-em-sources]] (the weak predicate requires this stated $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity, not the classical continuous-source regularity) and whose singular parts $(\rho_s,J_s)$ are point sources as in (b) or stationary-sheet sources as in (c), and let $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Say that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,J)$ when, for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$, the four pairings
$$\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle,\quad \langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$$
all vanish, all derivatives being distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields and the source pairings being those of (b) and (c). This clause defines a solution predicate. When the singular parts vanish, its four identities are the same as the locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. That earlier postulate explicitly excludes point and sheet distributions and does not imply their physical adoption here; adoption for the declared singular-source models is made separately, after this definition. No physical field equation is deduced merely from defining this predicate.

(f) [Scope] No product of two distributions is formed anywhere: the fields occur only through their distributional derivatives paired with a test function, and the source densities $\sigma,K$ occur only inside the ordinary surface and time integrals of (b) and (c); products such as $\rho_sE$ or $J_s\times B$ are not defined by this item. The definition asserts no existence theorem for fields with singular sources, no conservation law (continuity for these sources is proved separately where used), and no regularisation. Sources that are not locally integrable and are not point or stationary-sheet sources, moving sheets, line currents, and arbitrary products of distributions are outside the definition.
item.strategy: An explicit definition-contract item. Clause (a) is the regular-distribution identification. Clause (b) restates the pairings and the continuity theorem of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] with its properness hypothesis, and its finite-endpoint variant with the two endpoint deltas. Clause (c) defines the stationary-sheet pairings by explicit iterated integrals; well-definedness uses the finiteness of the surface measure of the compact $S$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]), continuity of $\sigma,K,\psi$ on compact sets and compactness of the time projection of the support of a test function, so both functionals are continuous of finite order on each test-support space. Clause (d) retains the unrestricted locally integrable field pair for the weak predicate, including sheet sources. It records optional interface hypotheses separately: joint one-sided spacetime C1 extensions support the pointwise branch; the weaker per-time spatial C1 trace branch needs the explicit piecewise-derivative and sheet-trace L1 hypotheses for its distribution/a.e. conclusions. Neither branch is a general weak-field admission condition, and separate spatial C1 traces alone are not claimed to give joint continuity or temporal bounds. Clause (e) defines the weak equations by the four vanishing pairings, with distributional derivatives of the regular distributions of the fields; the singular source terms enter only as the explicitly defined functionals of (b) and (c), never as products with the fields. Clause (f) records the exclusions; in particular the product of a singular source density with a field, which would be an undefined product of distributions, is not part of the definition. The vanishing-pairing clause is a precise mathematical solution predicate. It agrees with the old postulate on its original locally integrable source class, but does not extend that physical postulate deductively to singular sources; physical adoption is a separate postulate. It remains possible for a declared source pair to be incompatible with those equations, and no existence is asserted.

item.physical_scope: The distributional formulation of the Maxwell equations with point and stationary-sheet sources in a named inertial laboratory frame: the test-function pairings of moving point charges and of stationary sheets with charge density $\sigma$ and tangential surface current density $K$, and the unrestricted locally integrable field class for the weak equations. Joint one-sided regularity and the qualified L1 trace branch are optional interface hypotheses for pointwise or almost-everywhere jump conclusions, respectively. The item defines source objects and a weak-solution predicate; physical adoption of the singular-source equations is separate; it asserts no existence of fields, no conservation law, no self-force and no regularisation, excludes line currents, moving sheets and products of distributions, and carries the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the surface-measure interface.

item.title: Energy flow in crossed external fields with finite-volume accounting
item.statement:
Let $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$, $E_0>0$, and on $\Omega\times I=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ define, with $\theta(x,t):=kz-\omega t$, the frame $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]],
$$E(x,t):=E_0\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_1=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[E_0e_1e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr],\qquad B(x,t):=\frac{E_0}{c}\cos\bigl(kz-\omega t\bigr)e_2=\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\tfrac{E_0}{c}e_2e^{i(kz-\omega t)}\bigr].$$
The electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to one another and to the direction $e_3$ ('crossed' fields); $E$ oscillates along $e_1$, $B$ along $e_2$. Then:
(a) [Field data] $E$ and $B$ are smooth fields of [[def-em-fields]] on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and they satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho=0$ and $J=0$.
(b) [Energy density and flux] With $u$ and $S$ of [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]],
$$u(x,t)=\varepsilon_0E_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t),\qquad S(x,t)=\varepsilon_0cE_0^2\cos^2(kz-\omega t)\,e_3,$$
and the local balance $\partial_tu+\partial_zS_3=0$, equivalently $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}S=0$, holds exactly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.
(c) [Finite-volume accounting] For $a<b$, $L_1,L_2>0$ and the box $B:=(0,L_1)\times(0,L_2)\times(a,b)$ with outward normal $n$, for every $t$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{B}u\,dV=L_1L_2\bigl(S_3(a,t)-S_3(b,t)\bigr)=-\oint_{\partial B}S\cdot n\,dS:$$
the four faces with normals $\pm e_1,\pm e_2$ carry zero flux because $S$ is parallel to $e_3$, and the upper face $z=b$ has outward flux $L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and the lower face $z=a$ has outward flux $-L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$. Their respective signed contributions to the field-energy change are $-L_1L_2S_3(b,t)$ and $L_1L_2S_3(a,t)$.
(d) [Scope] The configuration is an ideal source-free plane wave, the finite-volume accounting of (c) is the fixed-volume energy balance of this declared solution in the sense of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]], and the example asserts nothing about the total energy of the field over all of $\mathbb R^3$ nor any empirical realization. $E_0>0$, $k>0$ and $\omega=ck$ are the declared parameters of the configuration.
item.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct substitution, with the oscillatory derivatives computed through the complex-exponential encoding of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]]. (a): the fields are of class $C^\infty$ because they are real parts of compositions of the linear map $(x,t)\mapsto i(kz-\omega t)$ with the entire exponential and of the real-linear projection, so the smooth calculus applies ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]); in particular, the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]) applied to $\exp\circ(i(kz-\omega t))$, with the real total differentiability and derivative of the complex exponential ([[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]], [[thm-complex-differentiability-real-linearity-wirtinger-and-cauchy-riemann]]) and Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta$ ([[thm-eulers-formula]]), gives $\partial_te^{i\theta}=-i\omega e^{i\theta}$, $\partial_ze^{i\theta}=ike^{i\theta}$ and, taking real parts, $\partial_t\cos\theta=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_z\cos\theta=-k\sin\theta$; substitution into the four smooth-branch equations verifies them with $\rho=0$, $J=0$ (both divergences vanish because the fields depend only on $z$ and have no $e_3$ component, curl $E=-\partial_tB$ and curl $B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$ reduce to the displayed scalar identities using $\omega=ck$). (b): $(E\times B)_3=\lvert E\rvert\lvert B\rvert=E_0^2c^{-1}\cos^2\theta$ by the orthogonal triad $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and $\lvert E\rvert^2=E_0^2\cos^2\theta$, $\lvert B\rvert^2=E_0^2c^{-2}\cos^2\theta$; with $1/(\mu_0c^2)=\varepsilon_0$ and $1/(\mu_0c)=\varepsilon_0c$ from [[def-em-si-conventions]] this gives the displayed $u$ and $S$; the product rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $\partial_tu=2\varepsilon_0E_0^2\omega\cos\theta\sin\theta$ and $\partial_zS_3=-2\varepsilon_0cE_0^2k\cos\theta\sin\theta$, whose sum vanishes because $\omega=ck$; this is the local identity of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] for $J=0$. (c): $u$ is continuous and independent of $(x,y)$, so [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] reduces $\int_Bu\,dV$ to $L_1L_2\int_a^bu(z,t)\,dz$; [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates that integral under the integral sign; the local identity and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\frac{d}{dt}\int_Bu\,dV=-L_1L_2\int_a^b\partial_zS_3\,dz=-L_1L_2(S_3(b,t)-S_3(a,t))$; the evaluation of the six face integrals uses only that $S=S_3e_3$ is independent of $(x,y)$. (d) records the scope; no empirical premise is used.

item.title: Localization of a continuous function by axis-parallel cube integrals
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the Lebesgue-measure interface used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $g:U\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. Suppose that $\int_Qg\,d\lambda_n=0$ for every closed axis-parallel cube $Q=\prod_{i<n}[a_i,a_i+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$ and $Q\subseteq U$, the integral being that of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. Then $g=0$ on $U$. In particular, for $n=2$, a continuous function on an open subset of the plane whose integral over every closed axis-parallel square contained in its domain vanishes is identically zero. The hypothesis requires all such cubes with every centre and every side length; a single cube or only the cubes centred at one fixed point do not suffice. For the latter restriction, on $U=\mathbb R^n$ the nonzero continuous function $g(x)=x_1-p_1$ integrates to zero over every cube centred at $p$ by cancellation in its first coordinate. This restriction differs from testing all cubes that merely contain $p$.
item.strategy: The Countable Choice convention is the Lebesgue interface of [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] and [[def-countable-choice]]. Suppose $g(p)\ne0$ for some $p\in U$; replacing $g$ by $-g$ if necessary, assume $g(p)>0$. By continuity at $p$ ([[def-metric-continuity]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) choose $\delta>0$ with $B(p,\delta)\subseteq U$ and $g(x)>g(p)/2$ whenever $d(x,p)<\delta$. The closed cube $Q:=p+[-\delta/(2\sqrt n),\delta/(2\sqrt n)]^n$ satisfies $Q\subseteq B(p,\delta)$, has side length $\ell=\delta/\sqrt n>0$ and satisfies $g\ge g(p)/2$ on $Q$. By [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], $\lambda_n(Q)=(2\delta/(2\sqrt n))^n=\ell^n>0$; the continuous $g$ is Borel measurable ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]) and bounded on the compact cube $Q$ ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]), so the signed integral over $Q$ is defined ([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). Monotonicity and the scalar rules ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]) give $\int_Qg\ge\int_Q(g(p)/2)\,d\lambda_n=(g(p)/2)\lambda_n(Q)>0$, contradicting the hypothesis $\int_Qg=0$. Hence $g(p)=0$ for every $p\in U$. The planar clause is the case $n=2$. No regularity beyond continuity, and no choice beyond $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is used.

item.title: Joint regularity of radial vector and scalar potentials on star-shaped domains
item.statement: Regularity convention for a possibly non-open parameter interval I: a map on $U\times I$ is jointly $C^k$ when it is the restriction of a $C^k$ map on some open neighbourhood $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ of $U\times I$; jointly $C^\infty$ means the restriction of one smooth map on such an open neighbourhood. For open I these are exactly the usual open-domain classes of def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms. At included endpoints of a nondegenerate time interval, time derivatives are the corresponding relative one-sided derivatives. For empty or singleton I the restriction convention still asserts extension existence and the stated spatial identities, but it does not determine time jets uniquely from the restricted values alone. This convention does not require a fixed uniform enlargement of an unbounded I. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a$, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$. Then the radial witness $A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B(a+s(x-a),t)\times(x-a)\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^k$ jointly with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ for every $t$, then the radial scalar witness $\phi(x,t):=-\int_0^1\langle C(a+s(x-a),t),x-a\rangle\,ds$ is $C^k$ jointly on $U\times I$ and $\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)$ for every $t$. For $C^\infty$ data both potentials are $C^\infty$ jointly. No global potential on an arbitrary open set is claimed.
item.strategy:
The interval regularity convention is supplied explicitly in the statement, rather than treating the imported open-domain definition as already covering non-open products. To prove regularity in that same extension sense, choose an open-neighbourhood Ck extension of the data (intersect the extensions' neighbourhoods if both B and C are used). Let P be the set of (x,t) for which every (a+s(x-a),t), 0<=s<=1, lies in that open extension domain. It contains UxI by star-shapedness. It is open: at any one point of P its compact radial segment has a finite cover by balls contained in the extension domain; equivalently its distance from the closed complement is positive, and continuity of the radial map uniformly in s keeps all nearby (x,t) segments inside those balls. The identical radial integral of the extension data is therefore defined on P and is Ck there by the compact parameter proof below; its restriction is the stated potential. For smooth input use its one smooth extension and the same argument through every finite order. Curl-freeness/divergence-freeness is only needed on the original slices to establish the field identities there, not on the enlarged neighbourhood. Set w=x-a and z_s=a+sw. The spatial star-shaped hypothesis puts z_s in U for 0<=s<=1. For any compact spatial box Q contained in U and compact parameter subinterval J contained in I, the radial image of [0,1]xQ is compact inside U. Each component of the vector and scalar radial integrands is a finite sum of products of the polynomial factors s,w and the Ck components of B(z_s,t) or C(z_s,t). Chain and product rules give every mixed spatial/time word derivative through total order k as a continuous function of (s,x,t) on the corresponding compact product. Apply thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle in each parameter coordinate, with others fixed, and induct on derivative order. Uniform continuity on the compact product and lem-uniform-integral-error-bound show that each resulting derivative integral is jointly continuous. Included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals use the relative endpoint derivatives of the compact-rectangle supplier. For empty or singleton I, construct the potentials using a chosen ambient extension on its open radial-admissibility set and restrict; this proves the same extension existence and spatial identities, without claiming uniquely determined time jets on the degenerate restriction. Thus both explicit integrals are jointly Ck, without assuming k+1 derivatives, and applying this for every k gives the smooth assertion. No surface-measure or Lebesgue integration/Choice branch of lem-em-parameter-integrals is needed: these are ordinary one-dimensional integrals in s on [0,1].

At each fixed t, the positive vector integral is exactly the witness of thm-a-divergence-free-c1-field-on-a-star-shaped-open-set-has-a-vector-potential, so curl A=B. For the scalar branch put Psi_C(x,t)=integral_0^1 <C(z_s,t),w> ds, and take phi_C=-Psi_C. The published Poincare theorem gives grad Psi_C=C; its convention is positive gradient, so it cannot itself justify grad of the positive integral being -C. Explicitly, curl C=0 means partial_j C_i=partial_i C_j in three dimensions. Differentiation gives partial_j Psi_C=integral_0^1 [C_j(z_s,t)+s sum_i w_i partial_j C_i(z_s,t)] ds. Replace partial_j C_i by partial_i C_j; the integrand becomes d/ds[s C_j(z_s,t)]. thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative gives C_j(x,t)-0*C_j(a,t)=C_j(x,t), hence partial_j phi_C=-C_j. Therefore grad phi_C=-C with the stated finite-k and smooth joint regularity. In particular for C=e1, phi_C=-(x1-a1), so grad phi_C=-e1; the old positive integral gave +e1 and was a concrete contradiction. Neither a general non-star-shaped global existence claim nor a new physical assumption is introduced. On a ball the same construction is local even when the surrounding open set has holes; scalar circulation and vector-flux obstructions remain distinct.

item.statement: Take $D=[0,1]^2$, $a\in C^2(I)$ with $a>0$, $r(u,v,t)=(a(t)u,a(t)v,0)$, $B=e_3$ and $v=(a'/a)(x_1,x_2,0)$. The parametrized flux is $a^2$, so its derivative is $2aa'$. item.title: A fixed smooth-domain extension that preserves smooth parameters
item.statement:
Let `Omega⊂R3` be a bounded smooth graph domain. Choose an open spatial neighbourhood `V` of its compact closure. There exists a fixed real linear spatial extension operator `E_Omega`, determined only by the domain, finite charts and cutoffs, with this parameter property. For every open interval `J` and function `u:Omega×J→R` that is smooth in the interior and whose every mixed derivative has a continuous extension to `closure Omega × J`, the function `E_Omega u` is `C∞` on `R3×J`, equals `u` and all its continuous boundary jets on `closure Omega × J`, and is supported spatially in one fixed compact subset of `V`. For every compact `K⊂J`, integer `m≥0` and `j≥0`,

$$\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j E_\Omega u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_m\sup_{t\in K}\|\partial_t^j u(\cdot,t)\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)}.$$

The `C^m` seminorm is the finite sum of suprema of spatial derivatives through order `m`. The extension commutes with every time derivative; charts and coefficients do not depend on `t`. No uniform bound over all of an unbounded `J` is assumed. Vector-valued inputs of finite dimension are extended componentwise. This construction adds no choice principle: a finite atlas can be selected from the cover of all admissible chart patches, finite cutoffs are supplied by the published finite-partition/cutoff lemmas, and the infinite coefficient sequence is defined explicitly below. The consuming elliptic/Sobolev argument retains its already-declared AC assumptions.
item.strategy:
**1. Explicit coefficients; no unproved moment lemma.** Put `b_k=−2^k`, `k=0,1,...`. For `N≥k` define

$$a_k^{(N)}=\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{1-b_j}{b_k-b_j},\qquad a_k=\lim_{N\to\infty}a_k^{(N)}.$$

The factors for `j<k` have sign negative, those for `j>k` positive; the sign is `(-1)^k`. For every finite index set, `prod(1+2^{-j})≤6`: the factors `j=0,1` give 3, and for the tail `j≥2`, the sum of `2^{-j}` is at most `1/2`, while the elementary induction `prod(1+x_j)≤1/(1−sum x_j)` bounds that tail by 2. Similarly `prod_{l=1}^M(1−2^{-l})≥1/4`: separate the first factor `1/2`, and use `prod(1−x_j)≥1−sum x_j≥1/2` on `l≥2`. The geometric-series supplier gives the stated sums, including their starting indices.

For `j<k` the absolute product is

$$2^{-k(k+1)/2}\frac{\prod_{j<k}(1+2^{-j})}{\prod_{l=1}^{k}(1-2^{-l})};$$

for `j>k` it is `prod_{j=k+1}^N(1+2^{-j})/prod_{l=1}^{N-k}(1−2^{-l})`. Thus

$$|a_k^{(N)}|\le576\,2^{-k(k+1)/2}\qquad(N\ge k).$$

At fixed `k`, the positive absolute value increases with `N`, since every new tail factor is greater than one, and it is bounded by this displayed constant. The published real monotone convergence theorem gives the limit `a_k`, with the same bound and sign. This defines every coefficient without selecting unspecified sequences.

For each integer `r≥0`, finite interpolation gives `sum_{k=0}^N a_k^{(N)} b_k^r=1` when `N≥r`: the polynomial

$$z^r-\sum_{k=0}^N b_k^r\prod_{\substack{0\le j\le N\\j\ne k}}\frac{z-b_j}{b_k-b_j}$$

has degree at most `N` and vanishes at the `N+1` distinct nodes `b_0,...,b_N`, so is zero by the exact published real-polynomial root bound; evaluate at `z=1`. To pass to the limit, the bound above gives `|a_k^{(N)} b_k^r|≤576·2^{-k(k+1)/2+kr}` uniformly in `N`. For `k≥2r+1` this is at most `576·2^{-k}`, whose tail tends to zero. First cut the sum at a fixed `M`, pass to the limit in those finitely many coefficients, and then let `M` increase. This proves both

$$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k b_k^r=1,\qquad\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|a_k|\,|b_k|^r<\infty\quad(r\ge0).$$

No original Seeley coefficient existence assertion is used as an unproved prerequisite.

**2. One flattened patch, with arbitrary parameters.** Write a smooth boundary patch as `(y,s)`, `s>0` inside the domain. A localized input `w(y,s,t)` has spatial support compactly inside the ambient chart, separated from its artificial edges, and every mixed derivative extends continuously to `s=0`. Extend it by zero at the artificial positive-side edges to the half-space. Choose a fixed smooth real normal cutoff `rho` that equals 1 near 0 and vanishes for `s≥delta/2`, with `delta` small enough that all sampled positive collar points remain in the chart. Define

$$\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=w(y,s,t)\ (s\ge0),\qquad\mathcal Ew(y,s,t)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\rho(b_ks)w(y,b_ks,t)\ (s<0).$$

For fixed negative `s`, the sum is locally finite because `b_k s=2^k|s|` eventually exceeds the cutoff support. It is therefore smooth off `s=0`. For any normal order `r`, tangential multi-index `alpha`, time order `j`, and compact parameter/tangential set, its termwise derivative for `s<0` is

$$a_k b_k^r\,[\partial_z^r\partial_y^\alpha\partial_t^j(\rho(z)w(y,z,t))]_{z=b_ks}.$$

On the fixed compact collar and a compact `K⊂J`, every input derivative in this formula is bounded; the supremum of the sum is bounded by a finite cutoff-dependent constant times `sum|a_k||b_k|^r`. The bounds hold locally uniformly up to `s=0`, with the **same** compact time set `K`; only the normal spatial argument is sampled.

As `s↑0`, for each fixed term the normal cutoff is identically one and all its positive-order derivatives vanish. The derivative therefore tends to `a_k b_k^r partial_s^r partial_y^alpha partial_t^j w(y,0,t)`. The finite-head/uniform-tail argument using the weighted absolute sum proves uniform convergence of the boundary limit on compact `(y,t)` sets. The moment identity then makes that limit exactly the input boundary derivative. This establishes matching continuous derivatives of every mixed order; no derivative of an infinite nonuniformly convergent series is assumed at the boundary.

**3. Matching jets imply actual joint smoothness.** For a function glued from the two sides, matching values give continuity. If the side first partial derivatives extend continuously and agree, the normal coordinate-segment FTC, on either side and up to `s=0`, proves the derivative at `s=0` equals their common limit. For tangential or time segments at `s=0`, first write the coordinate-segment FTC at `s≠0`, then let `s→0`; uniform convergence on the compact segment passes the integral to the common continuous boundary derivative. FTC again gives that tangential/time derivative on `s=0`. Thus the glued function is `C1` jointly. Apply the same argument successively to the already-matched derivatives of orders 1,2,... to obtain `C∞` on the ambient patch × `J`. The input itself obeys those boundary segment identities by the same limit from its positive side. This is a complete smooth-gluing argument, not a reference to a Whitney extension theorem.

The derivative bound at total spatial order `m` uses only input derivatives through `m`, with `sum|a_k|2^{km}` finite and the fixed cutoff derivatives through `m`. The operator is linear and does not change the time argument, so the time-commutation identity and the stated local seminorm estimate follow.

**4. Finite chart gluing on the fixed smooth domain.** Choose finitely many shrunk smooth graph charts and an interior open patch. Compactness gives finitely many smaller balls covering the domain closure, with their closed larger balls contained in the assigned chart/interior open members. Using the choice-free Euclidean compact cutoff supplier, take smooth nonnegative psi_l equal to one on each smaller ball and supported in its larger ball. S=sum_l psi_l is positive on a neighbourhood of the closure. Choose a smooth outer cutoff chi equal to one near the closure and compactly supported in {S>0}. For each chart j set chi_j=chi(sum of psi_l assigned to j)/S on {S>0}, and zero elsewhere. These functions are smooth, have supports in the chart members, and sum to one near the closure. Only finitely many choices are made; no measure-convention partition theorem is used. Localize u by these fixed spatial cutoffs. The interior piece is supported away from the physical boundary and is extended by zero, preserving smoothness. Each boundary piece is pulled through its smooth chart and extended by the preceding formula. Choose a fixed outer chart cutoff equal to one on both the positive localized support and the small negative support created by the extension, with compact support inside the larger chart; multiply before pulling back. This makes each piece smooth across its artificial edges when extended by zero in ambient space. Such collar sizes and cutoffs are available by shrinking the finite compact patches. The extension's tangential support never leaves that of the localized piece, and its negative normal support stays within `|s|<delta/2`, so the claimed outer support control is genuine.

Pullback is smooth by repeated ordinary chain rule with chart derivatives bounded at each fixed order on those compact supports. Add the finitely many pieces. On the domain their sum is `u` by the partition identity; all boundary jets agree by continuity from the interior. Each support lies in a fixed compact subset of the prescribed `V`, so their finite union does too. The charts, partitions and coefficient sequence are independent of time. This proves the claimed single parameter-preserving operator and its `C^m` seminorm bounds; it introduces no temporal patch choices or global bounds on unbounded intervals.

item.title: Smooth parameter-dependent Dirichlet and compatible Neumann Poisson solvers
item.statement:
Assume AC and Countable Choice carried by the variational/Sobolev suppliers. Let `Omega` be a bounded smooth graph domain in `R3`, `epsilon>0` constant and `J` an open interval. Let the bulk datum `f` be jointly smooth up to `closure Omega×J` in the all-mixed-derivative sense of the first supplier, and let boundary families `g_D`, `kappa` be smooth in a fixed finite boundary atlas × `J`. Then the Dirichlet problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `u|boundary=g_D` has a unique solution on `Omega×J`; it has a single smooth ambient continuation near the closed spatial domain × `J`. The Neumann problem `−epsilon Delta u=f`, `epsilon partial_nu u=kappa` has such a solution precisely when

$$\int_{\Omega_j}f(\cdot,t)+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)=0\quad\text{for each component and every }t\in J.$$

It is unique modulo a separately chosen spatial constant on each component at each time. The normalization `integral_Omega_j u(·,t)=0` gives a unique smooth family. Both solution operations are linear in their data; time differentiation commutes with them. Smoothness and estimates are local in compact time subintervals, with no uniform-in-`J` requirement. The smooth ambient continuations are auxiliary and are not unique off the closed physical spatial region.
item.strategy:
**Fixed boundary lifts.** Use a finite boundary partition, graph coordinates `r=x3−h(y)`, with the domain on `r<0`, outward normal `nu=(-grad h,1)/sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`, and a fixed normal cutoff equal to one near 0. On a localized boundary datum `g_j(y,t)`, the Dirichlet lift is `rho(r)g_j(y,t)` with a larger fixed chart cutoff. For an outward conormal datum `kappa_j`, the Neumann lift is

$$L_N\kappa_j(y,r,t)=\frac{r\rho(r)\kappa_j(y,t)}{\epsilon\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(y)|^2}},$$

again with a fixed larger chart cutoff equal to one near the datum support. At `r=0`, the terms from differentiating the coefficient or cutoff vanish because of the factor `r`, while `partial_nu r=sqrt(1+|grad h|²)`; hence `epsilon partial_nu L_N kappa_j=kappa_j`. Add the finite chart pieces. The partition's boundary sum is one, so both lifts have the exact required datum. They are linear, independent of time, smooth in an actual spatial collar × `J`, and their spatial `H^{k+2}` norms are bounded by constants times finite `C^{k+2}` boundary seminorms. Choosing higher seminorm orders is allowed; no sharp boundary Sobolev norm is asserted. For Dirichlet, subtract the lift and apply the earlier zero-lift weak Dirichlet solver plus the exact published higher-order Dirichlet estimate to the source `f+epsilon Delta L_Dg_D`.

**Neumann weak existence and H1 bound.** The earlier weak Neumann lemma accepts the bulk `L2` datum and the bounded boundary trace functional, and proves necessity/sufficiency of componentwise compatibility. Smooth boundary `kappa` defines that bounded functional by Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact published `H1→L2(boundary)` trace theorem. Mean-zero coercivity on each component gives

$$\|u\|_{H^1}\le C_{\Omega,\epsilon}\bigl(\|f\|_2+\|\kappa\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}\bigr)$$

for the normalized solution, by testing against it and absorbing the gradient norm. A bounded smooth graph domain has only finitely many components: every bounded open component has boundary in the domain boundary; a finite cover by connected one-sided graph patches meets only finitely many components, and every component meets such a patch. Thus all normalizations and lift/estimate sums are finite. After subtracting `H=L_N kappa`, the residual `w=u−H` has homogeneous Neumann flux and source `f+epsilon Delta H`; its mean is the negative mean of `H`. The smooth first Green identity verifies the weak lift subtraction, and the divergence theorem verifies that its residual bulk integral is zero under the original compatibility. A constant normalization does not affect the flux or elliptic equation.

**Natural-boundary H2 estimate; explicit source terms.** Flatten the fixed smooth boundary and take a localized weak solution `z∈H1` supported away from artificial chart edges, whose weak equation, for supported `H1` tests including nonzero boundary trace, is

$$\int A_{ij}\partial_jz\partial_iv=\int p v+\int G_i\partial_iv,\quad p\in L^2,\ G\in H^1.$$

The smooth symmetric uniformly positive transformed `A` is the ordinary Jacobian/metric transform of the constant scalar operator. The original homogeneous-flux problem has `G=0`; localization by a spatial cutoff `eta` changes the scalar datum to `eta p−A grad z·grad eta+G·grad eta` and the vector datum to `eta G+z A grad eta`, still respectively `L2` and `H1`. These exact terms account for natural flux under localization; no false zero-trace condition is imposed.

For a tangential direction `k`, put `w_h=delta_h^k z` and test with `v=−delta_{−h}^k(eta² w_h)`. This is a supported `H1` test, allowed by the natural variational formulation; it need not vanish at the physical boundary. The published quotient integration-by-parts/product/weak-commutation identities give principal term `integral eta² A(y+h) grad w_h·grad w_h≥alpha||eta grad w_h||²`. The coefficient/cutoff remainders are exactly those of the usual quotient expansion and are bounded by `C||z||H1 (||eta grad w_h||2+||w_h||2)`, with `||w_h||2≤C||z||H1` and `||delta_h A||infinity≤||partial_k A||infinity`. The scalar datum contributes at most `C||p||2(||eta grad w_h||2+||w_h||2)` because the derivative quotient stays on the test, not on `p`. Discrete integration by parts moves the quotient in the vector datum term to `G`, whose contribution is

$$\left|\int\delta_h^kG\cdot\nabla(\eta^2w_h)\right|\le C\|G\|_{H^1}(\|\eta\nabla w_h\|_2+\|w_h\|_2).$$

Cauchy–Schwarz and Young absorption give a uniform bound `||eta grad delta_h^k z||2≤C(||p||2+||G||H1+||z||H1)`. Pass to test pairings; the quotient's limiting derivative is a bounded functional on the `L2` closure of compact tests, and Hilbert Riesz supplies its `L2` representative. This provides all second derivatives with a tangential factor, including mixed ones, without a weak-subsequence assumption. The distributional equation is `−div(A grad z)=p−div G`; therefore the normal derivative has the corrected identity

$$A_{33}\partial_{33}z=-p+\operatorname{div}G-\sum_{(i,j)\ne(3,3)}A_{ij}\partial_{ij}z-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_iA_{ij})\partial_jz.$$

The right side is `L2` and `A33≥alpha>0`, giving the remaining derivative. Interior patches permit all quotient directions. Finite cover and the bounded chart pullbacks give the global natural-boundary `H2` estimate with the displayed data norms and `||w||H1`.

**Every higher order, without pretending Neumann derivatives keep zero flux.** If `w∈H^{k+1}` and its smooth homogeneous-Neumann equation has datum in `H^k`, localize as above; the localized scalar datum lies in `H^k`, and its vector datum lies in `H^{k+1}`. Tangentially differentiate by a multi-index `alpha` of order `k`. The resulting weak identity for `D_tan^alpha z∈H1` keeps principal matrix `A`, with scalar datum `D_tan^alpha p∈L2` and vector datum

$$D_{\rm tan}^\alpha G-\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}(D_{\rm tan}^\beta A)\nabla D_{\rm tan}^{\alpha-\beta}z.$$

This vector datum is `H1`: every commutator has at least one coefficient derivative, so it uses derivatives of `z` through at most `k+1`, all available from the induction hypothesis. The coefficient derivatives needed are bounded on the fixed smooth patch. The tangentially differentiated flux need not be zero: it is represented by these vector terms in the **natural weak identity**. The H2 estimate just proved applies to that identity. Tangential testing and differentiation are justified by supported smooth-up-to-boundary approximation; the published half-space extension and whole-space mollification/density interfaces provide the needed `H1` approximants without falsely using `H0^1` density.

This controls order-`k+2` derivatives with at most two normal factors. Expand the strong elliptic equation on the interior of each half-patch, differentiate at total order `k`, and recover successively target derivatives with three, four, ... normal factors by solving for the sole `A33` principal term. Every other derivative of order `k+2` has fewer normal factors; derivatives landing on coefficients use `z` through at most `k+1`. The source derivatives are `L2`. The identities represent global weak derivatives on the open half-patch because every compact test support lies in its interior. Finite cover closes the induction. Thus, for smooth data,

$$\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\le C_k\bigl(\|f\|_{H^k}+\|\kappa\|_{C^{k+2}(\partial\Omega)}+\|u\|_{H^1}\bigr),$$

where constants include the fixed geometry and `epsilon`. This sufficient, nonsharp estimate is complete for smooth parameter families and does not invoke a nonexistent published Neumann higher-order theorem.

**Strong equation and exact Neumann trace after regularity.** Once the estimates give all spatial orders, Sobolev embedding yields a $C^2$ representative on the closure. The weak equation tested against compact interior smooth functions makes the continuous residual $-\epsilon\Delta u-f$ vanish pointwise: if it had a nonzero value, continuity and a nonnegative bump supported in a small interior ball would give a nonzero test pairing. Apply the first Green identity to the smooth representative and tests obtained from the fixed smooth Dirichlet boundary lift. The weak Neumann identity then gives $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\epsilon\partial_\nu u-\kappa)q=0$ for every smooth boundary test $q$. If that continuous boundary difference were nonzero at some point, a nonnegative chart bump supported where it keeps one strict sign would produce a nonzero boundary integral (the smooth chart area Jacobian is positive). Thus the classical conormal equality is exact. This argument recovers the strong boundary condition from the natural weak formulation rather than presupposing it.

**Joint smoothness and the actual neighbourhood.** Differences and time derivatives of compatible data stay in the same compatible linear data space. Weak H1 continuity follows from the energy estimate. Applying the higher-order estimate to a difference quotient minus the solution for the derivative data makes that error tend to zero in every `H^m` on compact time patches, since bulk derivatives converge in `H^k`, boundary derivatives converge in the finite `C^{k+2}` seminorm, and the H1 error tends to zero. Induction gives all time derivatives as solutions for the differentiated data. Higher-order Sobolev embedding gives one consistent family of all mixed boundary jets; the first new parameter-preserving extension lemma then supplies a single smooth ambient continuation. Dirichlet families follow the same argument with the fixed Dirichlet lift and zero-trace operator. This proves both parameter branches of the second supplier.

item.title: Surface densities with vanishing test pairings vanish
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the surface-measure interface cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $S\subset\Omega$ be a compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], and let $a:S\to\mathbb R$ be continuous. If $\int_Sa\psi\,dS=0$ for every $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), then $a=0$ on $S$. Equivalently, if two continuous densities on $S$ pair equally against every test function, they are equal pointwise on $S$. The conclusion is pointwise and uses the continuity of $a$; a merely locally integrable density would satisfy only an almost-everywhere conclusion, which this statement does not claim.
item.strategy: Assume the stated Countable Choice convention. If $a(x_0)\ne0$, replace $a$ by $-a$ if needed and put $m=a(x_0)/2>0$. Continuity of $a$ on $S$ gives an ambient neighbourhood $N$ of $x_0$ on which $a\ge m$ on $S\cap N$. By the embedded $C^2$ hypothesis, the inverse/implicit-function suppliers give, after permuting coordinates, a graph chart $X(u)=(u,g(u))$ on an open $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ with $X(u_0)=x_0$ and $g\in C^2(D)$. Choose an open ambient chart neighbourhood $O\subset\Omega\cap N$ containing $x_0$, meeting $S$ only in this graph chart. Choose $0<r<R$ with $\overline B_R(x_0)\subset O$. The actual ambient bump supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] is a function $\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_R(x_0))$, $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(x_0)$; extended by zero it is in $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ by [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]. There is no product-extension assertion for arbitrary planar tests. By continuity of $X$, choose a closed nondegenerate parameter square $C\subset D$ around $u_0$ with $X(C)\subset B_r(x_0)$. The graph density is $J_X=\sqrt{1+|\nabla g|^2}\ge1$ by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]. The surface measure and restriction to Borel chart subsets are exactly those of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]; chart independence lets the integral of a function supported in $S\cap O$ be computed in this chart. Equivalently one may choose a compact Jordan region $C'\Subset D$, obtained as a finite union of closed parameter squares lying in $D$ and covering the compact parameter preimage of its support and use [[thm-surface-integrals-over-c-one-graphs]] followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] for the continuous graph integrand on $C'$. On the support of $\psi|_S$ we have $a\ge m$, and $\psi=1$ on $X(C)$. Consequently monotonicity gives $\int_S a\psi\,dS\ge m\int_{X(C)}1\,dS=m\int_C J_X\,d\lambda_2\ge m\lambda_2(C)>0$; [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]] gives $\lambda_2(C)=\ell^2>0$. This contradicts the given zero pairing. Every $x_0\in S$ therefore has $a(x_0)=0$, and applying this to the difference proves the equal-density clause. The compact embedded $C^2$ interface here is within the published compact embedded $C^1$ surface-measure class, with no change to its measure convention; in particular the closed stationary interfaces used by the jump theorem are covered. No new Choice principle is used. The empty-surface case is immediate.

item.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared distributional/surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
are required in $\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning that all four residual pairings defined there vanish for every compact smooth test. This is a physical adoption of the classical vacuum idealization in that source class, not a theorem about sources or a consequence of the original locally-integrable-source branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. When the singular part vanishes, the adopted identities coincide with that earlier weak branch.
Only source/field tuples satisfying these identities are models of this postulate; it does not assert existence for every prescribed source pair, and compatibility conditions remain consequences to be checked. Sources are the exact point and stationary-sheet types defined earlier, including their properness/endpoint and tangential-current qualifications. No moving sheet, line current, magnetic source, product of distributions, self-force, regularization, matter dynamics or material constitutive law is introduced. This postulate reports no experiment or measurement and does not infer empirical certainty from its mathematical formulation.

item.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
item.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the original locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source/field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the Countable Choice assumption of its defining source/surface-measure formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
item.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

item.title: A suddenly appearing point charge with zero current is inadmissible
item.statement:
Let $q\ne0$ be a real charge parameter (coulombs) and let $U:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the laboratory conventions of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. Define a distribution $\rho$ on $U$ by
$$\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_0^\infty\psi(0,t)\,dt,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$$
— an explicit switched-history distribution for $z(t)=0$ on $(0,\infty)$, with no compensating current or source contribution at the appearance event; it does not satisfy the proper-graph hypothesis of the zero-endpoint continuity branch of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) — and let $J:=0$ be the zero distribution. Then:

(a) $\partial_t\rho=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}$ and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), hence $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{(0,0)}\ne0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$: for every test function $\psi$, $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\,\psi(0,0)$, because $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth with compact support. In particular the continuity identity fails at the appearance event $(0,0)$.

(b) Consequently there are no locally integrable fields $E,B$ on $U$ satisfying the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair $(\rho,0)$ in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e): such fields would satisfy the distributional continuity identity of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b), which (a) contradicts. The source pair $(\rho,0)$ is therefore incompatible even with the formal four residual identities, and cannot be an actual source/field model under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]].

(c) The failure is exactly the omitted endpoint term of the point-source construction: by the endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]], the same trajectory on a bounded interval $I_0=(a,b)$ has $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=q\,\delta_{\gamma(a)}-q\,\delta_{\gamma(b)}$ with $\gamma(t)=(z(t),t)$. A switched point charge with $J=0$ and no endpoint or current term is thus inadmissible; a switched charge must be accompanied by an explicit current or endpoint source term, which the weak equations of [[def-em-weak-sources]] then require to satisfy continuity.

This is a mathematical incompatibility statement about a declared source model, not a report of a measurement: no apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty or empirical claim is involved.
item.strategy: Direct computation with the distributional definitions. (a) For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(U)$ the pullback $t\mapsto\psi(0,t)$ is smooth and compactly supported, so $\langle\partial_t\rho,\psi\rangle=-\langle\rho,\partial_t\psi\rangle=-q\int_0^\infty\partial_t\psi(0,t)\,dt=q\psi(0,0)$ by the fundamental theorem of calculus on the support interval ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]); the functional $\psi\mapsto q\psi(0,0)$ is $q\delta_{(0,0)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), which is nonzero because $q\ne0$ and some test function equals $1$ at $(0,0)$. Since $J$ is the zero distribution, $\operatorname{div}J=0$. (b) If locally integrable fields $E,B$ satisfied the four weak equations in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the distributional pair $(\rho,0)$, then [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) — stated for arbitrary distributional source pairs satisfying the four equations — would give $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(U)$, contradicting (a). (c) The endpoint clause of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] computes the endpoint deltas of a finite-history point source; setting $J=0$ while retaining the charge history $(0,\infty)$ is precisely the omission of those endpoint terms. Nothing here is a physical claim about charge creation: it states that the declared source model fails its own continuity requirement, and it exhibits the general statement of the previous item on an explicit example. The item inherits the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of [[def-em-weak-sources]], on whose clause (b) it depends, and records it in its dependencies; the computation itself is choice-free and uses neither the surface-measure interface nor any selection. The adopted physical singular-source equations are now supplied by [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; the original weak postulate excludes singular densities. The nonexistence proof is stronger than any source-admission question, since the four formal residual identities themselves imply the continuity that the switched history violates.

item.title: Stationary-sheet jump conditions of the weak Maxwell equations
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the interface and surface-measure definitions cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and source fields of [[def-em-sources]].

Let $S\subset\Omega$ be a fixed compact embedded $C^2$ hypersurface with a chosen unit normal $n$ pointing from the side $\Omega_-$ to the side $\Omega_+$ ([[def-em-surface-distribution]]), and let $\sigma:S\times I\to\mathbb R$ and $K:S\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuous with $K(x,t)\cdot n(x)=0$ for all $(x,t)$ (a tangential surface current density). Let $E,B$ be locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$ and $C^1$ on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ with the following explicit joint one-sided regularity: around every $(x_0,t_0)\in S\times I$, each side is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on an open spacetime neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller stationary graph cylinder. Thus the fields and their first space/time derivatives extend continuously to that side of $S\times I$, locally uniformly on compact cylinders, and let $\rho_v,J_v$ be continuous on $(\Omega\setminus S)\times I$ and locally integrable on $\Omega\times I$. Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces of such a field $F$.

Under the separate singular-source physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], suppose that $E,B$ satisfy the weak Maxwell equations with the source pair
$$\rho=\rho_v+\rho_S,\qquad J=J_v+J_S,$$
where $(\rho_S,J_S)$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with densities $\sigma,K$ and the pairings there, in the sense of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e), and where the volume parts $\rho_v,J_v$ are identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Then, pointwise on $S\times I$,
$$n\cdot[E]=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad n\times[B]=\mu_0K,\qquad n\cdot[B]=0,\qquad n\times[E]=0,$$
with the ordinary Euclidean inner and cross products of the one-sided traces ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]). Equivalently, the surface current density is $K=(\mu_0)^{-1}\,n\times[B]$ and the surface charge density is $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot[E]$.

The theorem assumes a stationary interface: the hypersurface $S$ and its normal do not depend on $t$, so the one-sided $C^1$ traces also make $\partial_tE$ and $\partial_tB$ locally bounded near $S$ and hence locally integrable, contributing no delta terms. No magnetic surface charge or magnetic surface current is present in the sources, and correspondingly the last two identities assert the absence of magnetic sheet delta terms. A moving interface, a normal sheet current, or a sheet whose support changes with time is outside this statement and would require additional terms.

[General weak trace branch] The weak Maxwell framework continues to allow the full locally integrable field/source class, without asserting undefined classical trace values. If instead of the joint extension condition the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time, assume in addition that their piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega\times I)$ and that their one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$. Then the same four jump identities hold as equalities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t\in I$. They hold at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. Merely having one-sided spatial $C^1$ traces separately at every time does not justify this last upgrade.
item.strategy:
First justify the spacetime use of the spatial supplier. For a compactly supported spacetime test $\psi$, let $K\subset\Omega$ be its compact spatial support projection and let $L\Subset I$ be a compact interval containing its time support. Choose finitely many spatial stationary graph neighbourhoods and interior open sets covering $K$. [[lem-finite-ambient-partitions-for-euclidean-boundary-integration]] gives smooth nonnegative spatial functions $\phi_j$ compactly supported in those sets with $\sum_j\phi_j=1$ near $K$. Explicitly, first choose finitely many nonnegative ambient bumps $\chi_j$ subordinate to that cover whose sum $s$ is positive near $K$; a cutoff $\theta\in C_c^\infty(\{s>0\})$ equal to one near $K$ exists by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], and $\phi_j=\theta\chi_j/s$ on $\{s>0\}$, extended by zero elsewhere, is smooth since $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ stays compactly inside the positive set. Their sum is $\theta=1$ near $K$, so $\psi=\sum_j\phi_j\psi$. This partition is independent of time, hence $\partial_t(\phi_j\psi)=\phi_j\partial_t\psi$ and temporal integration by parts acquires no partition derivative. On each spatial chart times $L$, the local joint one-sided extensions have a finite subcover of the relevant compact sheet-time subset, giving the compact bounds used below; interior compact supports are already covered by the ordinary joint $C^1$ assumption. In the joint branch the one-sided $C^1$ extensions and their derivatives are bounded on each compact closed half-cylinder, so the piecewise derivatives are locally integrable and the jumps are jointly continuous and bounded there. Apply [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]] to each component of the spatial slice at every fixed $t$ and integrate in $t$. The terms $F\partial_i\psi$, $(\partial_i F)\psi$ and $n_i[F]\psi$ are absolutely integrable on the compact support (the last uses the finite compact surface measure of [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]]), so [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] justifies integrating the identity. This gives $\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i[F_j]\delta_{S\times I}$, and contraction/antisymmetrization gives the divergence/curl formulas. For the temporal derivative, on each fixed spatial side, [[thm-integration-by-parts]] on a compact time interval containing the test support, followed by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], gives $-\int F_j\partial_t\psi=\int (\partial_tF_j)\psi$, with no endpoint term since the test support is compact in $I$. Integrate in $x$ by the same Fubini theorem. The sides are stationary, so no derivative of a moving spatial indicator occurs and $\partial_tF_j=\{\partial_tF_j\}$ with no sheet term.

The spatial sheet $S$ has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero: in each finite graph chart every normal section is a singleton, so Fubini gives zero volume, and the coordinate permutation preserves Lebesgue measure. Consequently $S\times I$ is locally four-dimensional null. Restrict each weak Maxwell identity to tests away from $S\times I$. The resulting ordinary residuals are continuous on the open complement, so the existing sign-and-ambient-bump argument forces them to vanish pointwise there. The ordinary residuals are locally integrable and differ from zero only on the null sheet, hence represent zero regular distributions by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]]. Subtract them to obtain the four sheet identities with densities $n\cdot[E]-\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\cdot[B]$, $n\times[E]$, $n\times[B]-\mu_0K$. For every spatial $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, each scalar component $H(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$ is continuous: on a compact time interval, joint continuity on the compact sheet gives uniform convergence as $t\to t_0$, and the bound $|H(t)-H(t_0)|\le S(S)\|\varphi\|_\infty\sup_{x\in S}|a(x,t)-a(x,t_0)|$ tends to zero. Testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ and using the one-dimensional sign-and-bump argument shows $H(t)=0$ at every time. Apply [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]] at that time and componentwise to get the four pointwise jumps. Tangentiality of $n\times[B]$ gives the stated current formula.

For the general weak trace branch, the additional local $L^1$ hypotheses on piecewise derivatives and traces justify the same Fubini arguments without compact uniform bounds. Temporal integration by parts is valid first on compact subintervals for each fixed off-sheet $x$, since the field is $C^1$ there; its integrable derivative and the test's compact support justify the integrated identity. The sheet residuals are therefore zero as distributions. For each fixed ambient spatial test $\varphi$, Fubini gives the locally integrable time function $H_\varphi(t)=\int_S a(x,t)\varphi(x)\,dS$, and testing $\varphi(x)\eta(t)$ shows its regular distribution is zero. The one-dimensional case of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] gives $H_\varphi(t)=0$ for almost every time. To obtain one exceptional time set, use the countable explicit ambient bumps with rational centres $q\in\mathbb Q^3$ and rational radii $0<r<R$ for which $\overline B_R(q)\subset\Omega$, equal to one on $\overline B_r(q)$ and supported in $B_R(q)$. They are defined by the fixed smooth-step formula in [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]], so no arbitrary choice of a test for each triple is needed. Remove the countable union of the null time sets for these tests, which remains null by [[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]. For a remaining time, a nonzero continuous spatial residual at any $x_0\in S$ has one strict sign on a sufficiently small graph neighbourhood. Density of the rationals ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]) gives one of those ambient balls wholly inside that neighbourhood whose inner ball contains $x_0$. A positive-area graph cell in its inner ball, as in [[lem-em-surface-density-localization]], makes its pairing nonzero, contradiction. Thus each residual vanishes at every spatial point for almost every time, which also proves the sheet-a.e. assertion. Joint continuity, if separately assumed, similarly upgrades to all times using positive-area cells times nondegenerate time intervals. The counterexample recorded in this proposal proves why this qualification cannot be omitted. All four electromagnetic conclusions and the unrestricted weak Maxwell framework are retained at their strongest justified regularity level; no Sobolev trace theorem or undeclared Choice principle is used.
