item.title: Evolution preserves the Gauss constraints
item.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$ ([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the Gauss defects
$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$
(a) Smooth evolution branch. Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$ $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only the two evolution equations
$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$
and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise. For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero initial Gauss defect.
(b) Distributional evolution branch. The same derivative conclusion holds for arbitrary scalar/vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in $\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). This includes the original locally integrable field/source branch identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$, assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral/localization interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is assumed.
(c) Full-Maxwell corollaries. Smooth solutions of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally-integrable weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point/stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise in (a) and distributionally in (b).
This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the continuous-representative localization and inherited declared singular-source formulation.
item.strategy:
(a) Smooth algebra. For $C^2$ fields, [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] give
$$\partial_tD_B=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tB)=-\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}E)=0,$$
and, with the positive commutation sign,
$$\partial_tD_E=\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=c^2\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)-c^2\mu_0\operatorname{div}J-\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=-\varepsilon_0^{-1}(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)=0.$$
Here $c^2\mu_0=\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ and the final equality is the separately assumed continuity, not a consequence of the evolution equations alone. The coordinate operators and product/linear rules are [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]. For fixed $x$, [[cor-mean-value-theorem]] on compact subintervals of $I$ proves constancy, propagation and nonzero persistence.
(b) The identical componentwise cancellation holds for distributions by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], whose derivative-commutation clause is choice-free: in $\sum_{i,j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}\partial_i\partial_jB_k$ the exchanged $i,j$ terms cancel. The two evolution identities and the independent continuity identity therefore give $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ without multiplying distributions.
For the continuous-representative conclusion, assume the stated Countable Choice and let $\partial_th=0$. Fix a spatial test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ and put $F(t)=\int_\Omega h(x,t)\varphi(x)d\lambda_3(x)$. On any compact time subinterval the integrands have fixed compact spatial support and a uniform bound, by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]] and [[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]. Hence [[thm-dominated-convergence]] makes $F$ continuous. All products with compact temporal tests are absolutely integrable; [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]], [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]] and [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] identify their multiple integrals with $\int_I F\eta$.
If $\eta\in C_c^\infty(I)$ has zero integral, extend it by zero and put $H(t):=\int_{-\infty}^t\eta(v)dv$. Equivalently start at a point strictly left of its support. The compact-test integral agrees with its Riemann integral by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], and [[thm-ftc-first-part]] gives $H\prime=\eta$. Since the total integral is zero, $H$ vanishes both left and right of the support interval; it is smooth and compactly supported inside $I$. Therefore $\Psi(x,t):=\varphi(x)H(t)$ is a legitimate compact test with $\partial_t\Psi=\varphi\eta$. Apply the derivative equation to THIS primitive test:
$$0=\langle\partial_th,\Psi\rangle=-\langle h,\partial_t\Psi\rangle=-\int_I F(t)\eta(t)dt.$$
Choose a real nonnegative compact bump $\beta$ in $I$ with integral one, using [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]] and the positive finite measure of an inner interval ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Decompose an arbitrary temporal test as $\eta_0=\eta-(\int_I\eta)\beta$. The preceding equality gives $\int_I(F-C)\eta=0$ for every $\eta$, where $C:=\int_IF\beta$. A continuous function with all such pairings zero vanishes pointwise: if a real or imaginary component is nonzero, continuity gives a subinterval where that component has one sign and is bounded away from zero; a nonnegative bump supported there, equal to one on a smaller interval, contradicts integral monotonicity ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). Thus $F$ is constant. The same argument for the continuous spatial difference $h(\cdot,t_1)-h(\cdot,t_2)$, now using bumps in $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, shows it is identically zero, since its pairing with every $\varphi$ is zero. This establishes independence of time. Compact support of every test, the actual derivative-test slot, and the public Countable Choice cost are explicit; no arbitrary-basepoint primitive is used.
(c) In the smooth full-Maxwell branch, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] supplies continuity, while Gauss gives $D_B=D_E=0$ directly; the original weak branch is the identical distributional argument. The separately adopted singular-source postulate uses the preceding solution predicate and the distributional continuity result. Conversely the propagated zero defects are exactly the missing two Gauss identities, so adding them to the evolution pair yields all four equations. No existence or empirical claim is inferred.

item.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$
and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions $t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch, and the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.
item.strategy:
(a) Differential implies integral. Fix $t\in I$ and a volume test geometry $V$; $E(\cdot,t)$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$, so [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies (the theorem assumes the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) and gives $\oint_{\partial V}E\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\int_V\operatorname{div}E\,d\lambda_3=(1/\varepsilon_0)\int_V\rho\,d\lambda_3$ by the Gauss law of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the same computation with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ gives the second identity. For a patch test geometry, [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]] applied to the $C^1$ fields gives $\oint_{\partial S}E\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS$ with the induced orientation of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and $\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS=-\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$ by Faraday's law. The flux function is $t\mapsto\int_D\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv$, a Riemann integral over the compact Jordan parameter region of a function whose time derivative $\langle\partial_tB(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ is continuous on a neighbourhood of $D$ times a compact interval around $t$; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this Riemann integral with the Lebesgue integral to which [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] applies, giving differentiability on $I$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB\cdot n_S\,dS=\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$. Combining gives the Faraday identity; the Amp\`ere identity is the same with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

(b) Integral implies differential. Fix a point $p\in\Omega$, an index $i$, and the cyclic pair $(j,k)$ with $e_j\times e_k=e_i$. For every closed box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subset\Omega$ with positive sides take its admitted open interior $V$. The volume identities and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] give $\int_V(\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0)\,d\lambda_3=0$. The integrand $h=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and bounded on $K$. The six faces of $K\setminus V$ are volume-null by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] applied to the positive and negative parts gives $\int_Kh=\int_Vh=0$. In particular this holds for every closed cube $K\subset\Omega$; [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] gives $h=0$ on $\Omega$. The same argument applied to $h=\operatorname{div}B$ gives $\operatorname{div}B=0$. For the curl components, take the affine patch $r(u,v):=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over the square $D_\ell=[-\ell/2,\ell/2]^2$ (a patch test geometry whose parameter region is a rectangle and whose normal is $r_u\times r_v=e_i$); the Faraday identity of (b), Stokes' theorem and the differentiability of the flux function give $\int_{D_\ell}\bigl(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB\bigr)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i\,dudv=0$ for every sufficiently small $\ell>0$. Because the identities hold for every affine square patch contained in $\Omega$, for each fixed coordinate plane every closed square in its open slice is covered (translate its centre to $p$); this is the hypothesis of the planar clause of [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] for the continuous function $u\mapsto(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i$ on the corresponding coordinate plane; hence $(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)\cdot e_i=0$ at every point of $\Omega$, for each coordinate $e_i$. The same argument with the Amp\`ere identity gives $(\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE)\cdot e_i=0$. Therefore the four equations hold pointwise. The argument shows why a single selected test geometry is insufficient: the recovery uses the full families of boxes and affine square patches of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the convention of the divergence theorem and the surface-measure interface.

item.title: Smooth scalar and vector potentials on a star-shaped space-time region
item.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and mathematical-prerequisites.md#M05; interfaces aligned to lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials and def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions
item.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; local second application of the published joint-regularity supplier; not an independent acceptance
item.statement: Let $c>0$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set that is star-shaped with respect to a point $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]). For any non-open time interval I, every joint regularity class here uses the open-neighbourhood restriction convention explicitly supplied by lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials, including the finite-k, C(k-1) and smooth conclusions. For the physical laboratory's open time interval the ordinary open-domain definition applies without extension. Fix an integer $k\ge2$ and let $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be fields of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-em-fields]]) satisfying the two source-free Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on $\Omega\times I$ in their pointwise form $$\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Then there are a scalar potential $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and a vector potential $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]) with $$B=\operatorname{curl}A,\qquad E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I.$$ If $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$, then $\varphi$ and $A$ may be chosen of class $C^\infty$ jointly. Conversely, if $\varphi$ and $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\operatorname{curl}A$ are their field pair, then $(E,B)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ on $\Omega\times I$. The theorem asserts existence on the stated star-shaped domain only: it claims no global potential on a general open $\Omega$, no boundary or decay condition on the potentials, and no uniqueness; potentials are auxiliary objects of the framework and not claimed to be observable.

item.title: Potential representations, gauge transformations and gauge equivalence of the framework's fields
item.design_state: explicit-definition-contract; class bookkeeping and the smooth group action are stated exactly; reachability is excluded by contract
item.statement: Let $c>0$, let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ with its restricted inertial chart be that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], let fields and units be those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let the potential-pair vocabulary (scalar-vector pair, field pair $E(\varphi,A),B(\varphi,A)$, Lorenz divergence $G$, Lorenz gauge, gauge transform $T_\chi$ and wave expression $W$) be that of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] on that region. (a) [Representations] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^{k-1}$ on $\Omega\times I$ and an integer $k\ge2$, a **potential representation of class $C^k$** of $(E,B)$ is a pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ whose field pair is $(E,B)$, that is, $\varphi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $A:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^k$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $$E=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA,\qquad B=\operatorname{curl}A\qquad\text{on }\Omega\times I,$$ the derivatives being those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. This definition asserts neither existence (supplied on star-shaped regions under their stated hypotheses by [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]]) nor uniqueness of a representation. (b) [Gauge functions and gauge equivalence] A **gauge function** of class $C^m$ ($m\ge2$) on $\Omega\times I$ is a function $\chi:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ of class $C^m$ jointly; its **gauge transformation** acts on a potential pair by $$T_\chi(\varphi,A):=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+\nabla\chi),$$ the transform of a $C^m$ pair being a potential pair of class $C^{m-1}$. Two pairs are **gauge related** when one is the transform of the other by some gauge function. On pairs and generators of class $C^\infty$, $T_0$ is the identity and $T_{\chi_1}(T_{\chi_2}(\varphi,A))=T_{\chi_1+\chi_2}(\varphi,A)$ for all $C^\infty$ generators $\chi_1,\chi_2$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], componentwise); hence gauge relatedness is an equivalence relation on the $C^\infty$ potential pairs. (c) [Conditions] A pair is **in Lorenz gauge** on $\Omega\times I$ when $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi=0$ there, and **in Coulomb gauge** in the chosen spatial chart when $\operatorname{div}A=0$ there. These are properties of a pair in the stated conventions. The existence of a gauge function achieving a condition, with or without prescribed initial or boundary data, is a separate PDE conclusion with its own hypotheses and is not part of this definition. (d) [Physical status] The physical content of a representation is its field pair $(E,B)$ of [[def-em-fields]]; the pair $(\varphi,A)$ and the gauge function are auxiliary, their values are convention dependent, and gauge related representations have the same field pair. The scalar potential carries the volt and the vector potential the tesla metre, consistently with [[def-em-si-conventions]]; no value of $\varphi$ or $A$ is by itself an observable or evidence for a field.
item.strategy:
A vocabulary and bookkeeping definition over the exact interfaces of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]; it makes no existence or solvability claim. Obligations checked: (i) the field-pair formulas and the transform are those of the cited definition, so the regularity statements (a $C^m$ pair gives $C^{m-1}$ fields; a $C^m$ generator gives a $C^{m-1}$ transform) are inherited exactly; (ii) the composition identity is the componentwise linearity of the coordinate partial derivatives, $\partial_t(\chi_1+\chi_2)=\partial_t\chi_1+\partial_t\chi_2$ and $
abla(\chi_1+\chi_2)=
abla\chi_1+
abla\chi_2$ ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), together with $T_0=\mathrm{id}$; the inverse of $T_\chi$ is $T_{-\chi}$, so the relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive on $C^\infty$ pairs; (iii) the definition deliberately separates the two gauge conditions from their reachability: no conclusion that a pair can be put in either gauge, with or without prescribed data, is drawn here (compare [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]] for existence of representations and the gauge-reachability theorem later on this page for the two declared branches); (iv) no choice principle, no domain hypothesis beyond the laboratory region, and no Maxwell equation is used.

item.title: Topological obstructions to global potentials: a curl-free loop field and a divergence-free sphere-flux field
item.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the vector obstruction is sharpened from C^2 to C^1 potentials by patch Stokes plus internal edge cancellation
item.statement: (a) [Scalar obstruction] On $U_1:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{(0,0,z):z\in\mathbb R\}$ the field $F(x,y,z):=(-y,x,0)/(x^2+y^2)$ is of class $C^\infty$, satisfies $\operatorname{curl}F=0$ on $U_1$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and is not the gradient of any $C^2$ function on $U_1$: its circulation around the positively oriented unit circle $\gamma(t)=(\cos t,\sin t,0)$, $t\in[0,2\pi]$, equals $2\pi$, since the pullback identity ([[lem-a-vector-line-integral-pulls-back-to-the-parameter-region]], [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]) gives $F(\gamma(t))\cdot\gamma'(t)=1$ by the sine and cosine derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]), and $\int_0^{2\pi}1\,dt=2\pi$ ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]); whereas for a $C^2$ potential $\varphi$ on $U_1$ the gradient theorem gives $\oint_\gamma\nabla\varphi\cdot d\mathbf r=\varphi(\gamma(2\pi))-\varphi(\gamma(0))=0$ ([[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]], [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]]). Hence a curl-free $C^\infty$ field on a connected open set need not have a global scalar potential, and the star-shaped hypothesis of [[pthm-em-spacetime-potentials]] cannot be dropped. (b) [Vector obstruction] On $U_2:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ the field $B(x):=x/\|x\|_2^3$ is of class $C^\infty$ and satisfies $\operatorname{div}B=0$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]), but there is no vector potential $A$ of class $C^1$ on $U_2$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$ ([[def-vector-potential-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). To see this, let $\Phi(\phi,\theta):=(\sin\phi\cos\theta,\sin\phi\sin\theta,\cos\phi)$ be the spherical parametrization, a regular patch on the rectangle $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ whose longitude seam and poles lie on the parameter boundary ([[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]], [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]); the flux of $B$ through the unit sphere in this orientation is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\langle B(\Phi),(\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta)\rangle\,d\phi\,d\theta=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\sin\phi\,d\phi\,d\theta=4\pi$, because $\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta=\sin\phi\,\Phi$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]]). Applying the classical Stokes theorem ([[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]]) to the two closed rectangular hemispheres $[0,\pi/2]\times[0,2\pi]$ and $[\pi/2,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$ ([[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], [[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-positive-orientation-for-elementary-region-boundaries]]) expresses the flux of $\operatorname{curl}A=B$ over each hemisphere as the circulation of $A$ around its induced boundary chain; in each hemisphere the two image meridian edges have the same image traversed in opposite directions and their integrals cancel ([[thm-line-integrals-under-reversal-and-concatenation]]), while the polar edge is degenerate, so the two circulations are the integral of $A$ over the equator and its reverse, cancelling each other; adding the two identities therefore gives $4\pi=0$, a contradiction. Consequently a divergence-free $C^\infty$ field on an open subset of $\mathbb R^3$ need not have a globally defined vector potential, and the star-shaped hypothesis of the potential theorem is substantive for the vector potential as well. (c) [The punctured space is simply connected] $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ is simply connected ([[def-simply-connected]]): it is path connected ([[def-path-connected]], [[cor-euclidean-spheres-are-path-connected]]), and every loop at every basepoint is null-homotopic. Indeed, for a basepoint $x_0$ with $\rho:=\|x_0\|_2>0$ the linear scaling $L(x):=x/\rho$ and its inverse are continuous bijections of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ ([[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]], [[thm-bounded-linear-operator-equivalences]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); a loop $\gamma$ at $x_0$ is null-homotopic if and only if $L\circ\gamma$ is, so it suffices to treat basepoints on the unit sphere. For $x_1$ on the unit sphere the radial homotopy $H(x,t)=((1-t)+t/\|x\|_2)x$ is continuous, fixes the unit sphere pointwise and deforms a loop at $x_1$ to a loop in the unit sphere ([[thm-radial-straight-line-map-on-punctured-rn]], [[lem-radial-normalisation-is-continuous]]); the loop in the unit sphere is null-homotopic rel basepoint there because $S^2$ is simply connected ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]), and composing that homotopy with the inclusion gives a null-homotopy in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ ([[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]). Thus the domain of the vector obstruction, unlike the domain of the scalar obstruction, admits no winding invariant, and simple connectivity of the domain is not by itself sufficient for the existence of a vector potential. (d) [Scope] The two obstructions have different characters: (a) is detected by the circulation of a closed loop, (b) by the flux through a closed surface. The fields displayed are smooth mathematical witnesses on the punctured open sets; the framework's postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] excludes magnetic charge, and no physical source, physical singularity or empirical claim is attached to them.
item.strategy: (a) Differentiate the components of $F$ by the quotient rule ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) to get $\operatorname{curl}F=0$; parametrize the unit circle, use the pullback identity for vector line integrals and the sine/cosine derivative and Pythagorean identities to get $F(\gamma(t))\cdot\gamma'(t)=1$, and evaluate $\int_0^{2\pi}1\,dt=2\pi$ by the fundamental theorem ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]). The gradient theorem for a $C^2$ potential gives zero circulation around the closed curve $\gamma$, so $F$ is not a gradient ([[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]], [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]]). (b) Compute $\operatorname{div}B=\sum_i\partial_i(x_i\|x\|_2^{-3})=3\|x\|_2^{-3}-3\|x\|_2^{-5}\sum_ix_i^2=0$ by the chain and product rules ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). For the flux, differentiate $\Phi$ to get $\Phi_\phi\times\Phi_\theta=\sin\phi\,\Phi$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]); since $B(\Phi)=\Phi$ on the unit sphere, the integrand is $\sin\phi$, and Fubini with the fundamental theorem evaluate the double integral as $4\pi$ ([[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). Suppose $A$ is $C^1$ on the open set $U_2$ with $\operatorname{curl}A=B$. Each hemisphere rectangle is a finite elementary Green region with its positive boundary chain and the spherical parametrization restricted to it is a $C^2$ regular patch whose image lies in $U_2$, so the classical Stokes theorem applies to each ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-positive-orientation-for-elementary-region-boundaries]], [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]]). In each hemisphere the induced boundary chain has four entries: one equator arc, two meridian arcs with the same image and opposite orientations, and one degenerate polar arc; the two meridian integrals cancel by reversal ([[thm-line-integrals-under-reversal-and-concatenation]]) and the degenerate one is zero. Hence the north circulation is the equator integral and the south circulation is its reverse, so their sum is zero; summing the two Stokes identities gives zero for the total flux of $B$ over the sphere, contradicting $4\pi\ne0$, and no such $A$ exists. (c) For the basepoint reduction, $L$ and $L^{-1}$ are linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$, hence bounded and continuous on the finite-dimensional space ([[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]], [[thm-bounded-linear-operator-equivalences]]), so a null-homotopy of $L\circ\gamma$ composed with $L^{-1}$ is one of $\gamma$; for a basepoint on the unit sphere, $H$ is the continuous radial homotopy of [[thm-radial-straight-line-map-on-punctured-rn]] fixing the unit sphere, so it deforms the loop to a loop in $S^2$ rel basepoint ([[def-homotopy-relative-and-path-homotopy]], [[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]), which is null-homotopic rel basepoint by simple connectivity of $S^2$ ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]); composing with the inclusion and concatenating gives the required null-homotopy in $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$. Path connectedness of $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ is seen by routing through the unit sphere ([[cor-euclidean-spheres-are-path-connected]], [[def-path-connected]]). (d) is the comparison of the two mechanisms: circulation versus flux. All suppliers are published items used at their stated hypotheses; no choice principle is used.

item.title: Gauge transformations preserve the field pair: invariance of the electric and magnetic fields
item.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with at least two elements ([[def-interval]]), $c>0$, and fix $k\ge2$. Let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ and let $\chi$ be a gauge function of class $C^k$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). Then the gauge transform $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(\varphi-\partial_t\chi,\ A+
abla\chi)$ is a potential pair of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly and its field pair is the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$: $$E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\qquad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I,$$ the common value being a map $\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ of class $C^{k-1}$ jointly (the field pair of $(\varphi,A)$ in the sense of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]). In particular, gauge related potential representations of a field pair ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]) have equal field pairs: the electric and magnetic fields are gauge invariants of the framework, and no value of $\varphi$, $A$ or $\chi$ is asserted to be observable. The identity uses only the definitions $E=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B=\operatorname{curl}A$, the vanishing of $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi$ for the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the equality of the mixed partials $\partial_t\partial_i\chi=\partial_i\partial_t\chi$; no Maxwell equation, no hypothesis on $\Omega$ beyond openness and no choice principle is used.
item.strategy:
Magnetic field: $\operatorname{curl}(A+
abla\chi)=\operatorname{curl}A+\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=\operatorname{curl}A$ by linearity of the curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]) and $\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0$ ([[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]], applicable because $\chi$ is $C^2$, indeed $C^k$ with $k\ge2$). Electric field: componentwise, $-
abla(\varphi-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(A+
abla\chi)=-
abla\varphi-\partial_tA+(
abla\partial_t\chi-\partial_t
abla\chi)$, where the bracket vanishes by equality of the mixed second partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and the componentwise linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ is [[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. Regularity: $\partial_t\chi$ and $
abla\chi$ are $C^{k-1}$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), so the transformed pair is $C^{k-1}$ and the two displayed field expressions are legitimate there; the common value equals the $C^{k-1}$ map $E(\varphi,A)$, resp. $B(\varphi,A)$, supplied by [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]. No further hypothesis is used.

item.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; explicit constant instance with the linear gauge function
item.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval ([[def-interval]]), and let $\chi:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ be of class $C^2$ jointly ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then the pair $$(\varphi,A):=T_\chi(0,0)=(-\partial_t\chi,\ 
abla\chi)$$ is a potential pair of class $C^1$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ whose field pair is the zero field pair: $$E(\varphi,A)=-
abla(-\partial_t\chi)-\partial_t(
abla\chi)=0,\qquad B(\varphi,A)=\operatorname{curl}
abla\chi=0\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I$$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the first identity by the equality of the mixed partials $
abla\partial_t\chi=\partial_t
abla\chi$ of the $C^2$ function $\chi$ and the second by [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]]. Explicit instance: for $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $ eta\in\mathbb R$ and $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x- eta t$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$, the pair is the constant pair $(\varphi,A)=( eta,a)$, with $E=-
abla eta-\partial_t a=0$ and $B=\operatorname{curl}a=0$ by [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. This pair is nonzero if and only if $( eta,a)
e(0,0)$; for $ eta=0$ and $a=0$ it is exactly the zero pair. To exhibit noninjectivity explicitly, take $ eta=0$ and $a=e_1=(1,0,0)$ on $\mathbb R^3	imes\mathbb R$. Then $(\varphi,A)=(0,e_1)$ and $(0,0)$ are distinct potential pairs with the same zero field pair. Thus the map from potential pairs to field pairs of [[def-em-fields]] is not injective: nonzero potentials may represent the zero field pair (pure-gauge fields), and no nonzero value of $\varphi$ or $A$ alone is evidence for a nonzero field, consistently with [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] and [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. The example is a statement about the representation of the zero field configuration; it asserts no Maxwell equation, no source configuration and no empirical situation.
item.strategy: Apply the gauge transformation $T_\chi$ to the zero pair $(0,0)$, using the linearity of the componentwise partial derivatives and of the gradient ([[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). The field pair of the zero pair is $(0,0)$; by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]] the transformed pair has the same field pair, which is $(0,0)$. The explicit formulas are then recomputed directly: with $\chi(x,t)=a\cdot x-\beta t$ one has $\partial_t\chi=-\beta$ and $\nabla\chi=a$, so $(\varphi,A)=(\beta,a)$; the fields of a constant pair vanish because every partial derivative of a constant is zero ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Both computations use only the definitions; no choice principle and no hypothesis on $\Omega$ or $I$ beyond openness and being an interval are used. The formula $(\varphi,A)=(\beta,a)$ includes all zero and nonzero parameter choices. Equality of this constant pair to zero is equivalent, component by component, to $\beta=0$ and $a=0$. Noninjectivity is established by the particular nonzero witness $a=e_1$, $\beta=0$, compared with the zero pair; it is not inferred by claiming that every parameter choice is nonzero.

item.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
item.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
item.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $ho:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega	imes I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,ho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG= rac{ho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+
abla G=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega	imes I$. (c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose additionally that the given potential pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega	imes I$. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations
$$W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$
The source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are automatic for a potential pair. For an arbitrary given $C^2$ potential pair, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge and these wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative. In full generality their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations in (a), including $-\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$. Thus the equivalence with decoupled waves holds within the declared Lorenz gauge, without asserting gauge reachability. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.
item.strategy:
(a) Componentwise expansion using the sum rules for divergence and curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]), the vector identity $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (c) Under the explicitly imposed hypothesis $G=0$, the continuously defined derivatives $\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$ vanish. Substitution in (a) turns the two sourced residual equations exactly into $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$. Conversely those two wave equations with $G=0$ make the residual equations hold, and the two source-free equations were already proved for every potential pair. There is no inference from Maxwell alone to a gauge condition; (d) is (b) with $G=0$ and $W\chi=0$. item.title: A homogeneous-wave gauge generator changes Lorenz potentials without changing their fields
item.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; explicit real cosinusoidal generator with |k| = omega/c
item.statement: Let $c>0$, let $k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega:=c|k|$, and let $$\chi(x,t):=\cos(k\cdot x-\omega t),$$ the real part of the complex plane wave $e^{i(k\cdot x-\omega t)}$ of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with wave vector $k$ and frequency $\omega=c|k|$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Then $\chi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and $W\chi=0$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ ([[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); indeed $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\chi$, $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\chi$ and $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$, so $W\chi=c^{-2}(-c^2|k|^2\chi)+|k|^2\chi=0$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Consequently, for every potential pair $(\varphi,A)$ of class $C^2$ jointly on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]]), the gauge-transformed pair satisfies $$G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G(\varphi,A)\qquad\text{and}\qquad E(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=E(\varphi,A),\quad B(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=B(\varphi,A)$$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ ([[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]], [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]); in particular, if $(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge then $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair. Explicitly $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$ and $\nabla\chi=-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, so $\varphi'=\varphi-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$, $A'=A-k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t)$; the zero pair is in Lorenz gauge and its transform $(-\omega\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t),\ -k\sin(k\cdot x-\omega t))$ is a nonzero pair that remains in Lorenz gauge and still represents the zero field pair. Thus the Lorenz condition does not determine the potential pair. The example is the residual generator $W\chi=0$ of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] on the free-space branch; on a bounded domain with prescribed gauge boundary data the admissible generators are restricted, and no such data-dependent claim is made here.
item.strategy: Compute with the chain and product rules: $\partial_t\chi=\omega\sin\theta$, $\partial_t^2\chi=-\omega^2\cos\theta$, $\nabla\chi=-k\sin\theta$ and $\Delta\chi=-|k|^2\cos\theta$ at $\theta=k\cdot x-\omega t$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substitute $\omega^2=c^2|k|^2$ to get $W\chi=0$. Then use the gauge-shift identity and field invariance of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]](b) and [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]; the class bookkeeping is that of [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. No choice principle is used and no boundary condition is imposed, matching the free-space branch of the gauge-reachability statement on this page.

item.reference: core-conditional-proofs.md#K7 and completed-expansion-arguments.md#W6; bounded-domain branch closed locally with the published elliptic resolvent and higher-order Dirichlet estimates; branch (b) parameter/ambient extension and compatible boundary-family estimates: physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-gauge-reachability-regularity-proposal.md
item.design_state: complete branch argument preserving the two Lorenz/Coulomb settings and restoring smooth parameter-dependent admissible Dirichlet/Neumann boundary data; incompatible data remain excluded
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in branch (a) and the Axiom of Choice together with $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as declared by its weak-solvability lemmas in branch (b) ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $c>0$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of the framework ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ and Lorenz divergence $G=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$. (a) [All-space slab; Lorenz gauge] Let $t_0<T$ and let $(\varphi,A)$ be of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (the restriction of a $C^\infty$ pair on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^\infty$ in the extension sense on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ with $\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_t\chi(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $W\chi=G$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$; the transformed pair $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, has the same field pair $(E,B)$, and any two such gauge functions differ by a solution of $W\chi=0$. This is the exact content of [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] read for potential pairs of the framework; its physical content is that every smooth potential representation of a field pair on a slab admits a Lorenz-gauge representative with zero gauge Cauchy data at $t_0$, without changing the fields. (b) [Bounded smooth domain; Coulomb gauge with admissible boundary families] Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ graph domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an arbitrary interval, possibly unbounded, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be $C^\infty$ on an actual neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$. Prescribe either (i) a Dirichlet family $g_D(p,t)$ smooth in boundary charts on a neighbourhood of $\partial\Omega\times\overline I$, or (ii) an outward conormal family $\kappa(p,t)$ with the same smoothness and the compatibility $\int_{\Omega_j}\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa(\cdot,t)\,dS=0$ for every connected component $\Omega_j$ and every $t\in I$. Then there is a gauge generator $\psi$, the restriction of one $C^\infty$ function on an actual open neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega\times\overline I$, such that $\operatorname{div}(A+\nabla\psi)=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. In case (i), $\psi(p,t)=g_D(p,t)$ on $\partial\Omega\times I$, and its restriction to $\Omega\times I$ is unique with those Dirichlet values. In case (ii), $\varepsilon_0\partial_\nu\psi(p,t)=\kappa(p,t)$ there, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}\psi(\cdot,t)\,dx=0$ for every component and every $t$ gives a unique generator on $\Omega\times I$; without that normalization it is unique modulo smooth time-dependent spatial constants on each component. The transformed pair $T_\psi(\varphi,A)$ is in Coulomb gauge and has the same physical field pair ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Any two Coulomb-gauge generators differ by a function spatially harmonic at every $t$; equal Dirichlet data eliminate that residual freedom, whereas equal Neumann data leave only the componentwise constants just described. Zero Dirichlet data are the corresponding special case. Auxiliary ambient continuations away from the physical region need not be unique. (c) [Residual freedom on star-shaped domains] Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and let $(\varphi,A)$, $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)$ be two potential pairs of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-interval]]) with the same field pair, both in Lorenz gauge. If I is non-open, these C2 classes and the resulting generator use the open-neighbourhood restriction convention of lem-em-joint-smooth-potentials; for the physical open laboratory interval they have their ordinary C2 meaning. If a degenerate I is used in this branch, choose the ambient C2 extensions as part of the data: the same-field and Lorenz conditions refer to these extensions on an ambient time neighbourhood before restriction, and their time jets are not determined uniquely by the restricted values alone. Then there is a gauge function $\chi$ of class $C^2$ jointly with $(\tilde\varphi,\tilde A)=T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ and $W\chi=0$ on $\Omega\times I$. (d) [Scope] Nothing is asserted about gauge functions meeting arbitrary prescribed boundary or initial restrictions: in (a) the gauge function has zero Cauchy data at $t_0$ and no spatial boundary condition or decay, and $\Omega$ is all of $\mathbb R^3$; in (b) the datum is either a smooth time-dependent Dirichlet family or a smooth outward conormal family satisfying the stated componentwise compatibility at every physical time, with zero-mean normalization for Neumann uniqueness; the older promise of a global Lorenz gauge on a bounded domain with prescribed boundary data is explicitly outside this result. The Coulomb-gauge statement concerns the spatial divergence in the chosen inertial chart, and the instantaneous appearance of the Coulomb potential is a property of the representation, not a signal: only the field pair $(E,B)$ is physical content ([[def-em-fields]]).
item.strategy:
(a) is [[lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability]] with its hypotheses and countable choice carried verbatim; the pair of the framework enters only through the vocabulary, so nothing is reproved. (b) The fixed-time smooth Dirichlet and compatible Neumann interfaces are those of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]], and their parameter-compatible ambient smoothness, exact boundary lifts, complete natural-Neumann estimates and normalized uniqueness are supplied by the earlier pure-mathematical [[lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers]]. Use the original open neighbourhood of the potentials and of the boundary family to choose an open time interval $J$ containing $\overline I$ by compactness of each fixed spatial/boundary fibre; only $\overline\Omega	imes K$, with compact $K\subset J$, is used for derivative bounds, never compactness of all $\overline I$. Put $F_t=\varepsilon_0\operatorname{div}A(\cdot,t)$. In the Dirichlet case the supplier constructs a fixed finite-chart spatial lift $H_t=L_Dg_D(\cdot,t)$ and the zero-trace operator $R$ for $-\varepsilon_0\Delta$ from its exact weak solver, including every $L^2$ source, with its higher-order bounds. Set $\psi_t=H_t+R(F_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta H_t)$. Differentiation includes the lift at every order: $\partial_t^j\psi_t=L_D\partial_t^jg_D+R(\partial_t^jF_t+\varepsilon_0\Delta L_D\partial_t^jg_D)$. Thus the spatial equation is $-\varepsilon_0\Delta\psi_t=F_t$ and the Dirichlet family is exact. In the Neumann case use the same supplier's compatible normalized weak solver and natural-boundary estimates. Compatibility is imposed only for $t\in I$: on an open $J$, define $c_j(t)=\int_{\Omega_j}F_t+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}\kappa_t$ and the auxiliary bulk extension $\widehat F_t=F_t-c_j(t)/|\Omega_j|$ on each of the finitely many components. It is smooth, compatible for all $t\in J$ and agrees with $F_t$ on $I$; no equation for the gauge outside the physical interval is promised. Apply the parameter solver to $(\widehat F,\kappa)$ with zero mean on each component. In either case locally uniform compact-time difference-quotient estimates give all mixed derivatives up to the boundary, and the supplier's fixed parameter-preserving Seeley construction supplies one actual ambient $C^\infty$ continuation, not merely separate finite-order Sobolev representatives. The resulting generator obeys $\Delta\psi=-\operatorname{div}A$ on every physical time, with the requested boundary data, so it is Coulomb gauge and preserves the fields by [[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]. Elliptic uniqueness gives the stated normalized uniqueness on $\Omega	imes I$; subtracting any two Coulomb generators gives $\Delta\chi=0$ and the listed Dirichlet/Neumann residual freedom. This argument retains the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses of the variational, chart and Sobolev suppliers, and imposes no global time bounds or extra regularity restriction. (c) Put $\delta\varphi=	ilde\varphi-\varphi$ and $\delta A=	ilde A-A$. Equality of the field pairs gives $\operatorname{curl}\delta A=0$ and $
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. Apply the corrected scalar lemma to $C=\delta A$ and denote its negative-gradient witness by $\phi_{\delta A}(x,t)=-\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds$. Then $
abla\phi_{\delta A}=-\delta A$ and $\phi_{\delta A}$ is jointly $C^2$. Take $$\chi_0=-\phi_{\delta A}=\int_0^1\langle\delta A(a+s(x-a),t),x-aangle ds,$$ so $
abla\chi_0=\delta A$. This additional negation is essential; using the lemma's negative-gradient witness itself as the gauge generator would reverse the vector-potential difference. Mixed partials of the $C^2$ function $\chi_0$ now give $
abla(\delta\varphi+\partial_t\chi_0)=
abla\delta\varphi+\partial_t\delta A=0$. For fixed t, restrict this $C^1$ scalar to each radial segment $a+s(x-a)$; the chain rule gives zero derivative, and cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant gives its common value $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)+\partial_t\chi_0(a,t)$. Since $\chi_0(a,t)=0$ for every t, the time derivative there is zero, so $h(t)=\delta\varphi(a,t)$ (in particular h is C1; indeed C2 under the stated hypotheses). For nondegenerate I, fix $t_*\in I$ and set $$\eta(t)=-\int_{t_*}^{t}h(u)du.$$ cor-primitives-of-a-continuous-function gives $\eta'=-h$ on I, with relative endpoint derivatives; since h is C1, eta is C2. Put $\chi=\chi_0+\eta$. Then $
abla\chi=\delta A$ and $\partial_t\chi=\partial_t\chi_0-h=-\delta\varphi$, so $T_\chi(\varphi,A)=(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)$. Finally the unchanged exact gauge-shift identity in pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form(b) gives $0=G(	ilde\varphi,	ilde A)=G(\varphi,A)-W\chi=-W\chi$, hence $W\chi=0$. The corrected radial construction gives chi0 as a C2 restriction from an open radial-admissibility neighbourhood. At the centre, the data extension gives h(t)=delta phi(a,t) on an open time neighbourhood; take the interval component containing I and construct the time primitive there. Adding this primitive to the chi0 extension yields a C2 extension on the intersection neighbourhood of Omega x I. Thus the asserted generator retains the same regularity convention at included endpoints of nondegenerate time intervals. Degenerate interval restrictions do not supply unique time jets: any use of this time-derivative branch there carries chosen ambient extensions and the same-field/Lorenz hypotheses on an ambient time neighbourhood, to which the nondegenerate construction applies before restriction. On an empty restriction there are no pointwise equations to prove. The physical laboratory branch already uses a nonempty open time interval.  This residual construction uses no choice principle; the preexisting Choice assumptions in branches (a)-(b) remain exactly as stated. The linearity of $
abla$ and $\partial_t$ used throughout is [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]; $H^m$ notation is [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and the elliptic problems use the domains of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. item.title: Surface independence of the total current flux and the role of the displacement term
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region $D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches; this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]
$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$
where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the displacement fluxes:
$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$
Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] The following declared smooth data satisfies all the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for $z\ge0$, and set
$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$
Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Take $D=[-1,1]^2$ and its interior $D^\circ=(-1,1)^2$. Let $\sigma$ be the standard smooth step of [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] and define $h(s):=\sigma(2(1-s^2))$, $\eta(u,v):=h(u)h(v)$. Then $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, $\eta>0$ at every point of $D^\circ$, and $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$ and outside $D$. Take the graphs
$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$
Both induced boundary chains are the square $\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region $V=\{(u,v,w):(u,v)\in D^\circ,\ -2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the patches, and
$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$
the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive.
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not an additional empirical claim.
item.strategy: (a) Put $G:=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$. By the smooth Gauss law and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], $\operatorname{div}G=\operatorname{div}J+\varepsilon_0\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho=0$ on that neighbourhood, the last equality being continuity, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applied to $G$ on the specified presentation of $V$ — outward normal $-n_1$ on the face $S_1$ and $+n_2$ on the face $S_2$ — gives $0=\int_V\operatorname{div}G=\int_{S_2}G\cdot n_2-\int_{S_1}G\cdot n_1$, which is the first asserted equality. The equality with $(1/\mu_0)\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r$ is Ampere's integral identity of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]](a) applied to either patch, whose induced boundary chain is $\gamma$; the two patches consequently give the same circulation. (b) Split $G$ in the equality of (a); this is algebra with the definitions of the fluxes ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) and no further analytic input. (c) Verify the smooth equations for the displayed data by direct substitution: $\operatorname{div}E=(t/\varepsilon_0)\chi'(z)$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$; $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}(E_z(z,t)e_z)=0$ because $E_z$ is independent of $x$ and $y$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB=0$; $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ and $\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE=-\mu_0\chi(z)e_z+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\chi(z)e_z=0$ since $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=\chi'(z)-\chi'(z)=0$. The standard step is smooth, is zero for arguments at most zero, is one for arguments at least one and is strictly positive on $(0,1)$ ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]]). Thus $h$ is smooth, positive for $|s|<1$, one for $|s|\le1/\sqrt2$ and zero for $|s|\ge1$; the product $\eta$ has exactly the declared properties. In particular the entire open square has positive graph separation, rather than merely a central subregion. Both graph maps are smooth and injective regular parametrizations on a neighbourhood of $D$, since their first two coordinates are $(u,v)$ and their area vectors are $(-\varphi_u,-\varphi_v,1)$. Their induced square boundary chains coincide at height zero. The explicitly restricted $V$ is nonempty, bounded and open, with compact closure contained in $[-1,1]^2\times[-2,0]$; its boundary is exactly $S_1\cup S_2$. Strict positivity of $\eta$ on $D^\circ$ gives $S_1\cap S_2=\partial D\times\{0\}$. This square seam is a compact union of four line segments, has surface measure zero on each regular graph face, and contains the relative face boundaries. At every point off the seam the boundary is locally the single smooth graph with $V$ above the lower graph and below the upper graph. The faces therefore give the actual finite presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]], with outward normals $-n_1,+n_2$, without overlapping positive-area face pieces. For $\varphi_1=-2\eta$, the induced upward unit normal is $n_1=(2\eta_u,2\eta_v,1)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$, so $(J\circ r_1)\cdot n_1=-\chi(-2\eta)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$; after multiplication by its area Jacobian the pullback density is $(J\circ r_1)\cdot(r_{1,u}\times r_{1,v})=-\chi(-2\eta)$. For the plane $n_2=e_z$ and the density is $-\chi(0)=0$. The graph flux formula thus gives exactly the two stated integrals, with the unit-normal scalar distinguished from the unnormalized area-vector density. On any ball $B(0,r)$ with $0<r<1/2$, $\eta=1$ and $\chi(-2\eta)=1$. The nonnegative continuous integrand has strictly positive integral on $D$, by the Riemann/Lebesgue comparison, monotonicity and positive ball area already declared; its negative is the strictly negative lower conduction flux, as stated. The total fluxes both vanish because $G=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE=-\chi(z)e_z+\chi(z)e_z=0$, consistent with the vanishing circulation of $B=0$. The explicit step-product supplies the required positivity on the entire square interior; the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the test-geometry, surface-measure and divergence-theorem items, and no further choice is used.

item.physical_scope: The surface-choice structure of the classical electromagnetic framework in a named inertial laboratory frame: for two oriented patches sharing a boundary loop and enclosing a region, the flux of the total current density $J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$ is the same through either patch and equals the circulation of $B$ divided by $\mu_0$, whereas the conduction-only flux may differ, its difference being carried by the displacement term; a self-contained smooth realisation is exhibited. The item is a conditional deduction from the adopted Maxwell equations and their continuity consequence; it asserts no experiment, no apparatus and no measurement, uses no idealised thin-wire current, and carries the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items.
